words.meaning: The basin-shaped bony structure at the base of the spine that connects the spine to the legs and surrounds organs in the lower abdomen.
words.pattern: the pelvis · a fractured pelvis · pelvic bones
words.cue: the bony basin below the waist
words.example: The ergonomics trainer explained how the pelvis supports the upper body when employees sit.
words.everydayExample: The anatomy diagram showed the pelvis below the spine.
words.usageNote: Pelvic is the adjective: pelvic bones, not pelvis bones. The pelvis is a structure, not a synonym for a single hip joint. Plurals: pelvises or pelves. This entry teaches language, not medical assessment.
words.recallPrompt: Describe where the pelvis is, using everyday language.

words.register: Neutral; medical; caesarean is usual in UK/Australian spelling, cesarean in US spelling
words.meaning: An operation in which a baby is delivered through surgical cuts in the abdomen and uterus; also an adjective describing that delivery.
words.pattern: have a caesarean / C-section · a caesarean birth · give birth by caesarean section
words.example: The employee-support guide used both caesarean and cesarean so colleagues in different regions could find the same information.
words.everydayExample: She told us that her baby had been born by C-section.
words.usageNote: These are spelling variants and an abbreviation for the same procedure, not three separate vocabulary items. Say have a C-section or give birth by C-section. Avoid implying that any method of birth is more legitimate than another; this is vocabulary, not clinical advice.
words.recallPrompt: Use C-section in a respectful, neutral sentence about a birth.

words.register: Neutral; meaning depends on the following noun
words.meaning: Receive money or property, especially by inheritance; also enter a place or begin a state in combinations such as come into effect, use, or contact.
words.pattern: come into money / an inheritance · come into effect / force / use · come into contact with
words.cue: receive, enter, or begin to apply
words.example: The revised supplier policy comes into effect on Monday.
words.everydayExample: She came into some money when her aunt died.
words.usageNote: Past: came into; past participle: come into. Come into money usually means inherit it, not earn a salary. Come into effect means begin to apply. In come into the room, the meaning is literal movement; learn the whole combination rather than assigning one definition to every occurrence.
words.recallPrompt: Make one sentence about inheritance and another about a policy starting to apply.

words.register: Neutral; especially useful for interpersonal feedback
words.meaning: Give other people a particular impression, whether or not that impression matches your intention.
words.pattern: come across as + adjective / noun phrase · come across as confident / dismissive / a good listener
words.example: A technically accurate update can come across as defensive if it ignores stakeholders' concerns.
words.everydayExample: He came across as shy at first, but soon relaxed.
words.usageNote: Use as before a description: she comes across as confident, not she comes across confident as. Come across something without as means find it by chance. Past: came across as.
words.recallPrompt: How can a leader sound decisive without coming across as dismissive?

words.register: Common in journalism and business; can suggest promotional hype
words.meaning: Promote or praise someone or something enthusiastically to encourage acceptance, attention, or sales.
words.pattern: tout a product / benefit · tout something as a solution · be touted as the next big thing
words.example: The vendor touted its platform as a cure for every planning problem, but the team asked for evidence.
words.everydayExample: The cafe touted its new brunch menu on social media.
words.usageNote: Being touted as effective does not establish effectiveness. Contrast endorse, which emphasizes support, and assess, which implies evaluation. Tout can also refer to soliciting business; in British English, a ticket tout resells tickets.
words.recallPrompt: Describe a product that is touted as transformative, without endorsing the claim.

words.register: Descriptive media language; sometimes critical, not a fixed technical term
words.meaning: Articles, videos, or posts about continually improving one's habits, productivity, fitness, or performance.
words.pattern: consume / create self-optimisation content · the pressure of self-optimisation
words.cue: media about making yourself ever more efficient
words.example: For the wellbeing campaign, we chose practical support over self-optimisation content that made rest sound like another performance target.
words.everydayExample: I stopped watching self-optimisation content before bed because even relaxing began to feel like a task.
words.usageNote: Self-optimization is the US spelling. Content is normally uncountable here: useful content, not many contents. Self-improvement content is a broader, often less efficiency-focused alternative. The phrase labels a topic, not an established clinical category.
words.recallPrompt: Explain when self-optimisation content helps you and when it creates pressure.

questions.prompt: Name the bony structure at the base of the spine that connects it to the legs: the ________.
questions.note: Pelvis is the noun; pelvic is the adjective.

questions.prompt: Complete the common abbreviation: Her baby was born by ________.
questions.note: C-section is short for caesarean section; cesarean is the US spelling.

questions.prompt: Complete the phrasal verb in the past: When her aunt died, she ________ some money.
questions.note: Come into money means receive it, especially by inheritance.

questions.prompt: Complete the collocation: The new policy comes into ________ on Monday.
questions.note: Come into effect or force means begin to apply.

questions.prompt: Complete the pattern: Her short reply came across ________ dismissive.
questions.note: Come across as describes the impression someone gives.

questions.prompt: Use today's promotional verb in the past: The vendor ________ the platform as a complete solution.
questions.note: Touted describes promotion, not proof that the claim is true.

questions.prompt: Use today's phrase for posts about continually improving habits and performance: I am taking a break from ________.
questions.note: This is a descriptive phrase; content is uncountable in this sense.

story.title: Support, not another target
paragraphs: A vendor touted its wellbeing app as a way to optimise every hour of an employee's day. Maya, an FMCG transformation director, noticed that most of its advice was self-optimisation content: track more, measure more, achieve more. She asked whether that was really the support employees needed.

A revised employee-support policy was due to come into effect the following month. Maya wanted its guide to come across as practical rather than preachy. An ergonomics section explained the position of the pelvis in plain language; a separate, professionally reviewed family-support section explained terms such as caesarean and C-section without giving individual medical advice.
The team replaced exaggerated promises with clear information and access to appropriate support. Rest did not need to become another performance target.
